To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following three architectural principles can be used to support a schema-less development approach in an RDBMS: (i) a JSON data type, (ii) an SQL/JSON language to query and index JSON data, and (iii) an SQL/NoSQL language to manage JSON data in the RDBMS.

we have identified three architectural principles that allow RDBMS users to manage JSON data in an RDBMS with a schema-less development approach and we have implemented these principles in industry-leading RDBMs.
the SQL/JSON approach provides a schema-less development approach within an RDBM system, which is an important requirement for applications that need to manage semi-structured data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a schema-less approach to JSON data management in RDBMSs, and we believe that the SQL/JSON approach is the most promising way to achieve it.

JSON is an excellent data format for the exchange of data between different applications and systems, but that RDBMS are still the best choice to manage data in an application.
SQL/JSON provides the best of both worlds: the flexibility of schema-less JSON data management and the power of the SQL language.
JSON data management is a natural extension to the relational database management system and that SQL/JSON provides an ideal solution for this.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SQL/JSON provides a single declarative query language that can be used for both relational data and flexible schema data.
SQL/JSON can be used for schema-less development.
the JSON data can be managed by the RDBMS with the same level of efficiency as relational data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the principles we propose are general enough to be applied to any RDBMS platform to support JSON.
it is feasible and relatively straightforward to add JSON support to an RDBMS.
the RDBMS can be extended to manage JSON data in a way that is consistent with its relational data management capabilities.
